source_en: Closed the flower stall early. Going home.
Going home. Residential block, second row.
Home to change the lilies' water.
Home from the stall. Nothing left to sell.
Going home to wait. The ceremony is soon.
I live at the end of the street.
Going home for lockdown. As instructed.
The stall is gone. Going home.
Returning to my residence. I have papers.
Meeting my florist. My bouquet is ready.
First visit. Staying with a cousin.
Buying my mother flowers. I never know which.
Buying a dress for the ceremony.
Taking supper to my husband and children.
Delivering roses. Business is very good.
Returning the wedding dress. Never liked it.
Anniversary dinner. Ten years married today.
Visiting from Varka. No address here.
My documents. Could we be quick? I have somewhere to be.
I keep my papers in the flowers. I forgot. No flowers today.
The dress is for a fitting. They asked me to wear it in.
I am going home. The ceremony is soon, I think. Soon.
I have always had my papers. The dress is for the wedding.
I know you. We have met. You waved at me once.
Thank you. There is a ceremony later. You should come.
I will remember your face. I remember every face.
Good. I knew you would understand. Not everyone does.
I am not sick. It is a dress. People wear dresses.
Is there a window? I like to see if it rains.
I thought… I was sure there was still time…
Will someone tell them… I tried to…
Where are you coming from?
The flower stall. Funeral lilies, mostly. I closed early to come home.
The stall. No flowers left. I arranged the empty buckets, then walked home.
Where the stall used to be. I stood there a while. Then here.
The bakery on Lenina Street. Six years at the ovens.
My new flat. I moved to the block last week. Still unpacking.
Home. My husband walked me to the corner. Married many years now.
Are you experiencing any symptoms?
No. Procedures I remember. Other things I lose. That is not a symptom.
I lose small things. Keys. Days. I wait up. I feel fine.
A little tired. I have been waiting a long time. That is all.
No. My memory is perfect. I have never lost a single thing.
A stiff neck from the dress. I bought it Monday. Brand new.
Nothing. I am not waiting for anything. There is no wedding. Never was.
Most people do not ask about the dress. You are not supposed to.
There is a ceremony soon. I am told to stay ready. So I am.
I asked someone what day it was. It was not the day I thought.
I have waited quite a while. A little longer is nothing.
Will it rain? The dress cannot get wet. It has been cleaned once.
I counted the days. I stopped when I lost count. It was high.
